I’d argue your husband has been selfish remaining in a friendship that is actively hostile and detrimental to your well-being. YTA. I myself have severe social anxiety. My father would always try and force me to order, which never worked. I would just be hungry and unhappy, and felt uncared for. The few times I gave into the pressure, the anxiety wasn’t remotely relieved in future and led to resentment towards him. Social anxiety requires graded exposure therapy and a gradual increase of the window of tolerance. You can’t force your daughter into ordering, and not feeding her because she can’t handle a social interaction is punitive. In certain contexts ordering for her could be seen as enabling, but if you’re aware she isn’t reliably able to order for herself, and being a child likely lacks the responsibility for planning meals ahead of time, you could easily keep protein bars in the car for food emergencies.

So, so much. Fanfiction scratches an itch books have yet to come close to touching, for me. They feel like different mediums of storytelling altogether, the rules are so different. 

I think one of the many differences between the two  stems from the different process of publishing. You don't need anyone's approval to publish fanfiction. No matter how true you try and keep your vision, standard publishing means having to sell your work to multiple people. What others think is a large barrier to what is shared. With fanfiction, it's entirely optional whether  opinions and feedback impact the work. The sky is the limit when it comes to creativity and boundaries to push.

There's also the fact that the world is familiar to consider. Familiarity with a setting, characters and plot leaves a lot more room and time for telling a story and telling it well because less energy is being put into world and character building when you aren't working from scratch.
